payload.name: observer-controller
payload.scope: To implement state-space control when not all states are directly measurable, by combining a state estimator with a state-feedback law into a single dynamic compensator.

definition.body: observer-controller is a human-authored control design methodology that combines a state observer with a state-feedback controller, using the observer's estimated states as inputs to the feedback law so that a complete control system can be built when not all states are directly measurable. Parameters: (1) an observer (typically Luenberger or Kalman) that estimates the state vector from available measurements; (2) a feedback gain law (e.g. u = -Kx_hat) that drives the estimated states toward desired values; (3) the combined dynamics where the observer and controller eigenvalues are distinct and the control law acts on estimated rather than true states. definition.body: structured-singular-value is a human-authored mathematical measure that quantifies the worst-case effect of structured matrix uncertainty on closed-loop stability. payload.name: loop-shaping
payload.scope: To shape the loop gain frequency response across bandwidth so that closed-loop systems meet robustness and performance specifications through frequency-domain design.

definition.body: Loop-shaping is a human-authored frequency-domain control design methodology that shapes the loop gain magnitude and phase response across frequency to achieve desired closed-loop performance and robustness specifications. The construct maps the trade-off between sensitivity attenuation at low frequencies, disturbance rejection at mid-frequencies, and noise sensitivity at high frequencies, parameterized by crossover frequency, bandwidth, and roll-off rate. The persistence mechanism: maintained as a core design procedure in classical and modern control (Skogestad and Postlethwaite; Zhou, Doyle, and Glover), taught in all control engineering curricula, and implemented in MATLAB loop-shaping design tools and mu-synthesis workflows. It is distinct from pole-placement (time-domain eigenvalue assignment, not frequency shaping) and from LQR (optimal quadratic design, not heuristic frequency shaping). e.g.: shaping loop gain for an aircraft pitch channel to achieve 30 deg phase margin and 10 rad/s crossover; loop-shaping of a DC-DC converter to reject 100 Hz line ripple while limiting high-frequency noise gain; hard-disk-drive servo loop shaped to reject mechanical resonances above 1 kHz | not: pole-placement (time-domain eigenvalue assignment, not frequency-domain shaping); LQR (optimal quadratic cost minimization, not heuristic frequency shaping); root-locus (analytical method for visualizing pole migration with scalar gain variation, not a synthesis procedure) [formal: modelatio loopae | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes]
